claims.text: The proposed alloy contains Ti and Ni as principal constituents plus at least three additional elements.
Each constituent is restricted to 5–35 at%, satisfying the stated HEA compositional definition.
The initial Ti–Ni-primary alloy can be produced as a fully homogenized single-phase or nearly single-phase solid solution by conventional processing.
A post-solidification aging treatment can nucleate and grow nanoscale coherent γ′-like precipitates in the Ti–Ni-primary alloy.
There is an aging temperature and time window that produces fine precipitates without excessive coarsening.
The aging temperature must be below the matrix melting point while being high enough to permit atomic diffusion.
The aging treatment will form uniformly distributed coherent nanoscale γ′-like precipitates in the Ti–Ni-rich matrix.
The coherent precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces provide precipitation strengthening.
Precipitation strengthening will raise the alloy's yield strength during elevated-temperature operation.
The aged alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the compositionally identical homogenized, unaged alloy.
The aged alloy will have greater creep resistance than the homogenized, unaged alloy.
The anticipated improvement in elevated-temperature yield strength will be significant, although its magnitude is not specified.
The intervention applies only when all alloying elements remain within 5–35 at% and Ti and Ni are the primary constituents.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or deleterious phase transformations would remove or reduce the intervention's benefit.
Precipitation strengthening is well established in systems related to the proposed Ti–Ni-primary HEA.
The exact aging temperature and time required for the proposed alloy are unknown and require experimental optimization.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant yield-strength improvement, or failure to observe the predicted fine coherent precipitates, would falsify the hypothesis.
